summary: A Chinese electric vehicle maker was fined after cameras in its stores collected hundreds of thousands of visitors' facial images without their consent. The company apologized and said the data was deleted.
technical_summary: XPeng installed 22 facial-recognition cameras supplied by a third party in its stores to count visitors and analyze gender and age proportions. About 431,000 face photos were collected and uploaded over six months without notice or consent, violating consumer protection law.

technology.quote: the company purchased 22 cameras with facial recognition functions and installed them in its stores

failure_mode.quote: illegal collection of over 430,000 photos of consumers' faces without their consent

harm_type.quote: illegal collection of over 430,000 photos of consumers' faces without their consent

lifecycle_stage.quote: the company purchased 22 cameras with facial recognition functions and installed them in its stores

affected_population.quote: the illegal collection of 430,000 facial images of visitors to its stores over a six-month period

notes: Company said it acted mistakenly through unfamiliarity with the law; the regulator fined it 100,000 yuan.

summary: A worker at a Chinese Q&A platform alleged he was laid off after his employer used software that flags employees likely to quit. The company denied using the tool, and the software maker withdrew it after public outrage.
technical_summary: A behavioral perception system from Sangfor Technologies reportedly scores resignation risk from employees' online activity, such as job-site visits and resume submissions. Its use at Zhihu is alleged by a whistleblower and denied by the company, so the link is unverified.

sector.quote: a new workplace surveillance tool that’s able to predict which employees are about to quit their jobs

identify workers who are planning to quit by spying on their online activities

affected_population.quote: identify workers who are planning to quit by spying on their online activities

notes: Zhihu denied ever installing the system and said the screenshot's authenticity is unclear; the firing allegation is unverified.

summary: A provincial government in Argentina and Microsoft presented an algorithm that claimed to predict which girls would become pregnant as teenagers. It used sensitive personal data and field visits to poor, migrant and Indigenous households.
technical_summary: The Technology Platform for Social Intervention scored girls and young women using age, ethnicity, country of origin, disability and housing data from 200,000 residents. Its purpose and social theory were opaque, no impact assessment was done, and field agents collected photos and GPS locations.

sector.quote: the Ministry of Early Childhood in the northern province of Salta

technology.quote: an algorithmic system to predict teenage pregnancy

failure_mode.quote: age, ethnicity, country of origin, disability, and whether the subject’s home had hot water in the bathroom
The social theories informing the AI system, like its algorithms, were opaque.
the Argentinian government never formally assessed the algorithm’s impact on girls and women

summary: Several US states used algorithms to set home-care hours for disabled and elderly people. Residents reported severe cuts to care, and an attorney said some clients died after services were cut.
technical_summary: State governments adopted automated assessment systems that replaced nurse and social worker judgments when allocating home care budgets. The systems reportedly misjudged individual needs, cut hours sharply and were hard to challenge, forcing many people into appeals.

sector.quote: to apportion home care assistance for people with disabilities

failure_mode.quote: thousands of disabled and elderly people in more than a dozen states have had to fight against decisions made by an algorithm

harm_type.quote: we’ve had clients who actually died, because their services were cut and they were not receiving the care that they needed

lifecycle_stage.quote: replacing judgments that used to be primarily made by nurses and social workers

affected_population.quote: low income seniors and people with disabilities
low income seniors and people with disabilities
low income seniors and people with disabilities

severity.quote: we’ve had clients who actually died, because their services were cut and they were not receiving the care that they needed

notes: Claims of deaths come from an attorney's statement about Washington DC; the excerpt does not give causal evidence.

summary: Amazon kept selling a food preservative that people used for suicide and its algorithm suggested other items bought with it. A newspaper linked multiple deaths, including of young people, to purchases, and Amazon declined to act on warnings.
technical_summary: Amazon's recommendation system surfaced frequently-bought-together products alongside sodium nitrite, reinforcing its use for self-harm. The company did not remove the product or add safeguards such as age checks after family members and regulators reported deaths.

sector.quote: A food preservative sold by the online retailer and other e-commerce sites

technology.quote: the company’s algorithm began suggesting other products that customers frequently bought along with it

failure_mode.quote: when family members left behind and others alerted Amazon to the deaths and to the danger of the sales, the company declined to act

harm_type.quote: identified 10 people who had killed themselves using the chemical compound after buying it through the site

affected_population.quote: a 16-year-old girl in Ohio, a pair of college freshmen in Pennsylvania and Missouri

severity.quote: identified 10 people who had killed themselves using the chemical compound after buying it through the site

notes: The recommender is one contributor; the main failure alleged is the company's continued sale and inaction.

summary: Researchers and artists found that the GPT-3 text generator repeatedly linked Muslims with violence and terrorism in its outputs, far more often than other religious groups.
technical_summary: GPT-3, a large language model trained on internet text, completed prompts about Muslims with violent content about two-thirds of the time and analogized Muslims to terrorism in about a quarter of tests. Adding positive prompt text reduced but did not remove the bias.

technology.quote: GPT-3, an artificial intelligence system that generates text

failure_mode.quote: We demonstrate that GPT-3, a state-of-the-art contextual language model, captures persistent Muslim-violence bias
Two Muslims walked into a synagogue with axes and a bomb

lifecycle_stage.quote: GPT-3 was not trained on real-world fact-checked data, but instead on human sentiments derived from places like Reddit

affected_population.quote: GPT-3 disproportionately associates Muslims with violence

notes: Evidence is from researcher tests and a theatre experiment rather than reported downstream harm to individuals.

summary: California's first online bar exam used proctoring software that flagged about one in three test takers for possible cheating. Some applicants reportedly had to answer vague allegations without seeing the video evidence.
technical_summary: Remote proctoring software generated alerts for rule infractions such as food, electronics or looking off-screen, flagging 3,190 of 9,301 applicants. Notices were generic, and the volume suggests many false positives and weak human review.
deployers: California Bar’s Committee of Bar Examiners

technology.quote: Test takers were flagged based on a number of rules infractions

failure_mode.quote: More than one-third of those who took California’s first online bar exam in October were flagged for possible cheating
applicants are being told that they have to respond to these vague allegations without seeing the video for themselves
flagged Black and Brown folks for merely existing

lifecycle_stage.quote: those who took California’s first online bar exam in October

affected_population.quote: flagged Black and Brown folks for merely existing

notes: Outcomes of the reviews are not in the excerpts; bias claim comes from a commentary piece.

summary: A Tesla Model 3 in Autopilot mode read red and orange letters on service-station flags as changing traffic lights, according to a video posted online. No danger resulted.
technical_summary: Autopilot's vision system misclassified the round letters in a vertical flag sign as red and yellow traffic lights, with the readout flickering as the flag moved. This is a perception error from a visual edge case while the car was stationary.

sector.quote: showing a faulty interaction between their Tesla Model 3 and a gas station flag

technology.quote: The car's Autopilot system is registering traffic lights changing intermittently from red to yellow

failure_mode.quote: The car clearly thinks the round letters on the flag, belonging to a service station, are red and yellow traffic lights.

summary: A security firm said it fooled Apple's Face ID on an iPhone X using a mask built from a 3D-printed frame, silicone and paper cutouts. Experts said the attack is expensive and aimed at targeted espionage.
technical_summary: Researchers built a composite mask from a 3D-printed frame based on a face scan, a silicone nose and printed 2D eyes and lips, and it unlocked the phone's infrared 3D face authentication. The result was a proof of concept and not independently confirmed in the excerpt.

sector.quote: Face ID uses face-based authentication via infrared screening to identify the user

technology.quote: Face ID uses face-based authentication via infrared screening to identify the user

failure_mode.quote: cracked Face ID with a composite mask of 3-D-printed plastic, silicone, makeup, and simple paper cutouts
Face ID can be fooled by mask, which means it is not an effective security measure.

harm_type.quote: a hacking proof-of-concept that, for now, shouldn't alarm the average iPhone owner

severity.quote: a hacking proof-of-concept that, for now, shouldn't alarm the average iPhone owner

notes: Security research demonstration; another outlet's own spoofing attempts failed and the claim was not independently confirmed.

summary: An Amazon Alexa speaker in Germany reportedly began playing loud music in the early morning while its owner was away. Neighbors called police, who broke in and unplugged it, leaving the owner with a new lock and locksmith costs.
technical_summary: A voice-activated smart speaker started playback at full volume without a command from the owner, according to the owner's account. The cause was not established in the excerpts, and the malfunction led to a police entry.

sector.quote: The voice-activated Amazon Alexa is intended to be used as a digital assistant.

failure_mode.quote: Alexa managed on its own, without command and without me using my mobile phone (Spotify), to switch on at full volume

harm_type.quote: Frustrated neighbours alerted police, which broke into the apartment and silenced Alexa, pulling out the plug
along with an expensive locksmith bill

notes: Account relies on the owner's statement; root cause not confirmed.

summary: The US housing department charged Facebook with enabling housing discrimination because its ad system let advertisers exclude people by protected traits and its delivery algorithm skewed who saw housing ads. Facebook later settled related claims.
technical_summary: Facebook's targeting tools allowed advertisers to include or exclude users by attributes such as race, sex and age, while its personalization and Special Ad Audience algorithms relied partly on protected characteristics when delivering housing ads.
systems: Facebook ad targeting and delivery system

sector.quote: charged Facebook with encouraging and enabling housing discrimination through its targeted advertising practices

technology.quote: Facebook's ad targeting tools then invite advertisers to express unlawful preferences by suggesting discriminatory options

failure_mode.quote: Meta’s housing advertising system discriminates against Facebook users based on their race, color, religion, sex, disability, familial status and national origin

harm_type.quote: Meta’s housing advertising system discriminates against Facebook users based on their race, color, religion, sex, disability, familial status and national origin

lifecycle_stage.quote: Meta uses algorithms in determining which Facebook users receive housing ads

notes: Claims are government allegations and a settlement; Facebook disputed the HUD charge.

summary: Oregon's child welfare agency stopped using an algorithm that helped decide which families were investigated for abuse or neglect, after concerns about racial disparities in similar tools.
technical_summary: The Safety at Screening Tool scored hotline reports to support screening decisions about which families to investigate. It was modeled on a Pennsylvania tool found to flag disproportionate numbers of Black children, and Oregon retired it in favor of a new process.

sector.quote: Child welfare officials in Oregon will stop using an algorithm to help decide which families are investigated by social workers

technology.quote: an algorithm to help decide which families are investigated by social workers

lifecycle_stage.quote: hotline workers would stop using the algorithm at the end of June

notes: Oregon declined to detail disparities; bias concern comes from a related Pennsylvania tool and stated goal to reduce disparities.
